The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Live updates: Bitcoin whipsaws between $81,000 and $84,000 as altcoins slide. Bitcoin bounced back from an early dip as ZEC, HYPE and SOL led altcoin losses. JPMorgan fell after kicking off U.S. earnings season. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin diverges from South Korean stocks as AI concerns deepen the Kospi selloff. South Korea’s chipmakers lead another sharp selloff as concerns over AI spending and Chinese competition grow, while bitcoin holds well above its summer lows. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ledger says 'spy' chip inside CryptoBilis Ledger devices transmitted wallet keys over mobile network. The hardware-wallet maker gave its first public account of how a covert component in devices sold by CryptoBilis could steal users’ master keys without changing Ledger’s software. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

UK court ruling boosts government’s chances of keeping $5 billion in seized bitcoin. The decision concerns 61,000 BTC seized by the Metropolitan Police in its investigation into Zhimin Qian, who pleaded guilty to defrauding thousands of people in China. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin whale that sat through the March 2020 crash moves $378 million. A bitcoin whale that received coins days before the Covid crash and sat through it has moved millions on-chain. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Tokenized SanDisk bets saw more liquidations than XRP as Asia’s chip rout wipes out $800 million. About $800 million in leveraged positions were wiped out over 24 hours, 86% of them bullish. Chip-stock contracts on crypto exchanges took a chunk of the damage. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $83,272 with a -0.21% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,494.79 with a -2.27% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.description:

items.title: US Crypto Policy Tracker Regulatory Developments
items.description:
On April 4, 2025, the SEC’s Division of Corporation Finance (the Staff) published a Statement on Stablecoins clarifying that in the Staff’s view the offer and sale of certain dollar-backed stablecoins does not involve an offer and sale of securities requiring registration under the US federal securities laws (the Stablecoin Statement). The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On December 16, 2025, the FDIC issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (the Proposal) to implement Section 5 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act). The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

Read more on Latham’sGlobal Fintech & Digital Assets Blog. [...] On April 1, 2026, the Treasury issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM), seeking public comment related to its implementation of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (the GENIUS Act), a comprehensive framework for the federal regulation of payment stablecoins enacted on July 18, 2025.

items.description:
Regulatory trends

Stablecoin legislation

In July 2025, President Donald Trump signed the GENIUS Act legislation into law, requiring stablecoins to be backed 1-to-1 by the US dollar or other low-risk assets. The United States has also enacted the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, which prohibits Federal Reserve banks from establishing or issuing a US CBDC.

SEC and CFTC crypto clarity [...] Hong Kong has introduced a dedicated stablecoin issuer licensing regime under the HKMA and FSTB. It proposes high-quality reserve-asset backing, segregation and custody requirements, independent audits, clear redemption rights, and governance standards. Algorithmic stablecoins and unbacked arrangements will face restrictions.

ETF & tokenized-asset guidelines [...] Stablecoin payment rules in the UK are still in development and have not yet come into force. The government has outlined a future framework in which stablecoins used for payments would be subject to requirements on backing, redemption, and issuer governance, with payment-system regulators gaining expanded supervisory powers over systemic arrangements. items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress passed legislation to establish a clearer framework for stablecoins and digital asset markets.

## Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs [...] Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress made progress in 2025 toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. One measure—the GENIUS Act—was signed into law. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.

## How cryptocurrency is regulated in the U.S.

items.description:
Stablecoins are moving to the center of global crypto regulation, with 12 G20 economies addressing them through existing or proposed legislation. The US, Canada, Japan, the EU, and the UK are advancing dedicated rules.

Both emerging-market and advanced economies still lag on comprehensive regulation and oversight. 36 of the 75 countries studied have regulations for taxation, AML/CFT, consumer protection, and licensing. 15 of the emerging markets studied have all the above regulations.

items.description:
Hyperliquid (HYPE) is a Layer 1 blockchain built to host a crypto-focused perpetual derivatives market. Investors initially used the Hyperliquid app to speculate on Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other crypto-only investments. But the technology was so slick—easy to use, instant settlement, 24/7 trading, etc.—that it quickly expanded to other markets. Today, nearly half the volume on Hyperliquid is in conventional assets like oil, silver, and the S&P 500. It’s expanding into spot commodities, [...] I suspect the coming bull market will be big enough to lift most of the sector. I’m bullish on the majors—Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, etc.—and on crypto equities. But there are two types of investments I think are particularly well positioned.

1. The Hyperliquid Lane: Crypto Financial Applications With Real Revenues and Good Tokenomics [...] Article cover image

# HYPE, HOOD, And The Next Crypto Bull Market

Matt Hougan

Matt Hougan@Matt\_Hougan·

Crypto is finally showing signs of a bottom. Since July 1, bitcoin is up 9%, even as the Nasdaq-100 is down 6%. ETF flows are turning positive, and sentiment is improving. While it’s too soon to sound the all-clear, it’s promising enough that I’m starting to get questions about what comes next.
